GET /affiliates/overview, GET /affiliates/resources, GET /affiliates/resources/{key}/file (routes/affiliates.py, backend/subscription/affiliates.py, affiliates_config.py). Gated by the DB flag affiliates (off/on, default off; uniform 404 before auth when off). The caller is resolved only from the session: the session user's account email must equal (case-insensitive) the owner_email of an active, non-deleted creator code on an active creator, otherwise 403 with no data (no client-supplied id exists). Responses are aggregates only: active paying subscribers (referred buyers with a subscriptions row status='active', non-free, price_cents > 0; trials excluded), monthly earnings = commission_rate x summed monthly plan price, new/total referred subscriptions per day/week/month (UTC), and milestone flags. Reached tiers are persisted once in affiliate_milestones (keyed by owner email) so churn never un-earns them; payouts stay manual. Tunables (commission rate 0.20, recurring for the life of each paying subscription, milestone tiers/bonuses, series lengths, link format, rate limit, resource manifest) live in api/config/affiliates.json. Resource files are copied from data/ into api/assets/affiliates/ by scripts/sync_affiliate_assets.py because the image contains only api/. Note: signup does not verify email ownership, so "verified email" is the account email on the authenticated session.

Promo codes (task 20260930-creator-friend-codes, phase 1: web/Stripe). Creator codes (admin-created, linked to a creators row) and friend invite codes (one per user, generated on demand) give a new individual subscriber the configured PROMO_DISCOUNT_PERCENT (50) off their first month. Code: backend/subscription/promo.py (config, PromoManager), routes/promo.py (user + admin endpoints), checkout/webhook hooks in routes/subscription.py, coupon + Stripe history lookup in stripe_service.py.

  • Config (env, eagerly validated by validate_promo_config() in the lifespan, no defaults, all three places: local .env, server ~/fellowscript-docker/.env (and legacy ~/fellowscript/.env), CI env in build-push.yml): PROMO_CODES_ENABLED (true/false; deploy false), PROMO_DISCOUNT_PERCENT (1-100), PROMO_VALIDATE_RATE_LIMIT (e.g. 10/minute). Set these on the server BEFORE deploying or the app refuses to boot. Enabling the flag is a manual decision.
  • Flag off: all /promo/* and /admin/promo/* routes return a uniform 404 before auth; checkout ignores promo_code and is not rate-limited by the promo limit.
  • Stripe model: DB is authoritative. One shared coupon fellowscript-first-month-{pct}pct (percent_off, duration=once) is created lazily and applied via discounts=[{coupon}] at session creation; promo_code_id rides in session/subscription metadata. No per-code Stripe promotion codes. Pricing stays server-side (price_for).
  • Rules enforced server-side (PromoManager.evaluate, run at validate AND at checkout creation): code normalized (trim/uppercase, case-insensitive), active, not expired, under max_redemptions, creator active, not the caller's own friend code, member_count == 1, TRIAL_MONTHS == 0 (no stacking), and buyer is a new subscriber: no subscriber_history, no stripe/apple non-free plan, not on a paid plan, no prior redemption (admin_comp and the free plan do not count), plus a Stripe lookup of customers by email with any non-incomplete subscription => ineligible. Any error, missing email, or ambiguous Stripe pagination denies. Buyer eligibility is computed before the code lookup so timing does not reveal whether a code exists. Every failure yields the same {valid:false} (validate) or 400 invalid_promo_code (checkout).
  • Redemption logging: only in checkout.session.completed, before the plan upsert (so a retry is not mistaken for a returning subscriber). Logged only if payment_status == 'paid', total_details.amount_discount > 0, individual plan, not self-referral, and no prior local paid history. PromoManager.log_redemption locks the code row, conditionally increments redemption_count (cap), inserts with ON CONFLICT (idempotency_key) DO NOTHING and rolls back on a replay, so retries never duplicate or double-count. Over-cap at webhook time is stored with over_cap=true for admin review; the purchase is not reversed. Errors 500 so Stripe retries. Typing a code or abandoning checkout logs nothing.
  • Refunds/cancels: log-only; rows are kept. Friend link: SITE_URL/?code=CODE, carried through signup by the frontend, always re-validated server-side. Audit: admin mutations emit admin_audit lines (ids only); logs never contain code text or emails.
  • Admin: endpoints only (require_admin), no admin UI.

Phase 2 (iOS) proposal, not implemented. Apple forbids client-only discounts for digital subscriptions, so the web mechanism cannot be reused. Option A, offer codes: Apple generates redeemable codes per creator in App Store Connect; users redeem in the App Store (or via presentCodeRedemptionSheet). Pros: no signing server, Apple handles eligibility and abuse. Cons: no in-app text field flow of our own, codes are generated in bulk in App Store Connect, friend codes (per user, dynamic) are impractical, and our DB cannot be authoritative for cap/expiry. Option B, server-signed promotional offers: the app sends a code to our server; the server runs the same PromoManager.evaluate, then returns an ES256 signature (key from App Store Connect, keyIdentifier, nonce, timestamp, productIdentifier, offerIdentifier, applicationUsername = a per-user token) that StoreKit 2 uses via Product.PurchaseOption.promotionalOffer. Pros: one DB-authoritative code system for creators and friends, same rate limit and fail-closed rules. Cons: Apple promotional offers are for existing/lapsed subscribers only (not new ones), so a first-month discount for brand-new subscribers is not expressible this way; new-subscriber discounts on iOS must use introductory offers (configured in App Store Connect, not per code) or offer codes. Recommendation: use offer codes (Option A) for creator codes on iOS (creator-specific code batches give attribution), attribute redemptions through App Store Server Notifications (OFFER_REDEEMED/SUBSCRIBED with offerIdentifier, handled in apple_service.py and /subscriptions/apple/notifications, logging a promo_redemptions row with platform='apple', idempotency_key = the transaction id), and treat friend codes as web-only until a signed-offer-eligible use case exists. Eligibility follows Apple subscription-group rules. Needs a separate decision and build before any iOS work. Separately, removing the iOS introductory trial in App Store Connect is a flagged manual follow-up; web and iOS trial behavior diverge until then.

Owner rewards (task 20261001-promo-owner-rewards). The owner of a code earns a reward worth OWNER_REWARD_PERCENT (50) off their NEXT month. Code: backend/subscription/owner_rewards.py (config, RewardManager, fail-closed entry points), apple_service.sign_promotional_offer, stripe_service.apply_owner_reward, routes in routes/promo.py, hooks in main.py signup flows and routes/subscription.py. Behind its own flag, deploy OFF; requires PROMO_CODES_ENABLED=true when on.

  • Config (all env, no defaults, eagerly validated by validate_owner_rewards_config() in the lifespan, three places: local .env, server ~/fellowscript-docker/.env + legacy ~/fellowscript/.env, CI env in build-push.yml; the app refuses to boot if any is missing/invalid, including with the flag off): OWNER_REWARDS_ENABLED, OWNER_REWARD_PERCENT (1-100), OWNER_REWARD_EXPIRY_DAYS, OWNER_REWARD_CAP_COUNT + OWNER_REWARD_CAP_WINDOW_DAYS (max rewards earned per owner per rolling window), OWNER_REWARD_MAX_OUTSTANDING (max earned-unclaimed per owner), OWNER_REWARD_IP_CAP_COUNT (max signup rewards credited per client IP per window), OWNER_REWARD_CLAIM_RATE_LIMIT, OWNER_REWARD_APPLE_RESERVATION_MINUTES, OWNER_REWARD_HASH_SALT (>=16 chars, HMAC key for email/IP hashes), APPLE_PROMO_KEY_ID, APPLE_PROMO_KEY_PATH, APPLE_PROMO_OFFERS (JSON {productId: offerIdentifier} covering exactly the 8 products: after the price cut the codes are the versioned invite_reward_50_v2 for ...access.one, invite_reward_50_v2_2 .. _8 for two..eight, created at 50% of the new Apple prices by apple_price_and_promos.py promos; the legacy unversioned invite_reward_50[_N] offers were at 50% of the old prices and are deleted after the env switch. The validator already accepts any [A-Za-z0-9_]{1,64} id, so no code change was needed. The three places are updated together at the env-switch step of the runbook; the CI value in build-push.yml already uses the v2 codes), plus the existing APPLE_BUNDLE_ID. The .p8 (SubscriptionKey_G6DRYNCNRS.p8, gitignored) is read only when the flag is true (must be an EC P-256 PEM; errors name the exception class, never key bytes). Putting the key on the production server is a manual step needing explicit confirmation; do it before enabling the flag there.
  • Flag off: every new route returns a uniform 404 before auth (POST /admin/promo/creator-codes, GET /admin/promo/codes-overview, POST /admin/promo/codes/{id}/deactivate, POST /admin/promo/codes/{id}/reactivate, DELETE /admin/promo/codes/{id}, GET /rewards/{user_id}, POST /rewards/{user_id}/apple/claim); signup/purchase hooks do nothing, so no rewards accrue.
  • Ledger (owner_rewards, source of truth): earned -> claimed | expired; idempotency_key UNIQUE (signup:<invitee id> / purchase:<Checkout Session id>); partial unique indexes allow one signup reward per invitee account and per invitee normalized-email hash (survives account re-creation); Apple claim_ref (transaction id) unique. Expiry is lazy (expires_at checked on every operation). Audit trail: append-only promo_audit_log (ids and reason codes only: earned, skipped_*, denied_self_referral, claimed, apple_signed, expired, admin code create/deactivate) plus the admin_audit log line.
  • Earn triggers: (a) invite_code (optional field on /signup, /auth/google, /auth/apple) naming an active friend code, run after account creation; (b) a 'logged' (within-cap) creator-code purchase redemption rewards the user whose account email equals the code's owner_email (must resolve to exactly one user). The owner must hold an individual (max_members=1), active, paid Stripe/Apple plan as its host at earn time; free, admin_comp, group, trialing or lapsed owners get nothing and the reward is dropped, not held (audited). Both hooks swallow errors (no reward, signup/webhook unaffected). Trigger (a) swallows errors (no reward, signup unaffected). Trigger (b) is retry-safe, see Retry-safe purchase crediting below. (c) a logged friend-code Stripe Checkout purchase (task 20261004-web-friend-invite-rewards) credits the inviter via earn_purchase -> _earn_friend_purchase, from the signature-verified checkout.session.completed webhook only (never at checkout creation), for web invitees who enter the code at Checkout without having signed up with it. It uses source signup and the shared signup:<invitee id> key plus the per-invitee/per-email unique indexes, so signup-with-code AND redeem credits the inviter once total, in either order; replays are no-ops. Same eligibility as (a) (paid individual owner plan, caps, self-referral denial, fail closed). The webhook has no client IP, so the per-IP cap is not applied on this path (the redemption already requires a paid, discounted first purchase by a buyer with no paid history). Behind the same OWNER_REWARDS_ENABLED flag; no new env var.
  • Abuse mitigations: one reward per invitee account and per normalized email (lowercase, +tag dropped, Gmail dots folded) via unique indexes; self-referral blocked (same user or same normalized email); per-owner cap per window and max outstanding; per-IP cap (HMAC-hashed client IP; no device identifier exists at signup, so IP + email normalization is the available dedupe); caps and insert run under Postgres advisory locks (IP then owner) so concurrent signups cannot exceed them; the signup endpoint keeps its 5/minute limit.
  • Stacking: rewards queue FIFO, one applied at a time (one per billing month).
  • Stripe owner (automatic): apply_owner_reward attaches the shared once-off coupon fellowscript-owner-reward-{pct}pct to the owner's Stripe subscription (next invoice) and the row is marked claimed in the same transaction (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED); subscription metadata owner_reward_id makes a crash-then-retry recognize its own prior apply. It defers (reward stays earned) if the subscription is not active, is set to cancel, or already carries any discount. Re-attempted on earn and on every customer.subscription.updated for an active sub (a renewal consumes the previous coupon, then the next reward queues). No new Stripe webhook event types are needed.
  • Apple owner (claim in app): POST /rewards/{user_id}/apple/claim (authenticated owner, rate-limited) requires an earned unexpired reward and an Apple individual subscription whose product is in the offer map; it reserves the oldest reward (fresh nonce, one outstanding signature per owner, else 409) and returns keyIdentifier, nonce, timestamp, signature (base64 DER ES256), productIdentifier, offerIdentifier, applicationUsername. Signed string: bundleId, keyId, productId, offerId, applicationUsername, nonce, timestamp joined with U+2063. applicationUsername is the claim's own nonce (a fresh lowercase UUID per signature); the client sets it as the purchase appAccountToken (StoreKitManager already uses the response's applicationUsername, so no iOS change), which makes the verified transaction echo the nonce back. See Apple double-claim protection below. The reward flips to claimed only when a verified Apple transaction with offerType == 2 and a mapped offerIdentifier arrives via /subscriptions/apple/sync or an App Store notification (OFFER_REDEEMED/DID_RENEW/SUBSCRIBED; notification DB errors 500 so Apple retries), idempotent on the transaction id, and only when its appAccountToken equals a reward's current ledger nonce. An unredeemed signature blocks a re-claim until it is provably dead (below). GET /rewards/{user_id} returns counts and can_claim_apple (the legacy per-user apple_application_username field is still returned for client decode compatibility but is no longer what gets signed).
  • Retry-safe purchase crediting (task 20261001-owner-rewards-security-fixes). Before, credit_purchase_reward swallowed errors and the checkout.session.completed replay returned early once the redemption row existed, so one transient DB failure permanently dropped a legitimate reward. Now _log_promo_redemption returns (code_id, buyer_id) whenever the session has a counted (not over_cap) redemption on record, whether logged just now, by an earlier delivery, or by a concurrent one (PromoManager.get_redemption reads the stored row). The webhook then calls credit_purchase_reward AFTER the buyer's plan upsert, so a crediting failure can never block the buyer's activation. credit_purchase_reward logs the exception class and re-raises; the webhook's existing except turns that into a 500 so Stripe re-delivers, and the replay re-attempts crediting. Idempotency: the reward key is purchase:<Checkout Session id> (UNIQUE, ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING under the per-owner advisory lock); earn_purchase also checks the key up front so replaying an already-credited purchase is a clean no-op (no spurious reward_skipped_* audit, no double-grant, concurrent deliveries yield exactly one reward). Fail closed is unchanged: ineligible/permanent outcomes (no owner, owner not subscribed, cap, self-referral, over-cap redemption, unknown code) return normally, grant nothing and the webhook answers 200 (no retry loop). Webhook replay is the reconcile path; no new route or cron exists. Residual: the Stripe discount application (apply_stripe_reward) stays best-effort and leaves the reward earned for the next customer.subscription.updated. Example: delivery 1 logs the redemption, crediting hits a DB blip, webhook 500; Stripe retries, the redemption exists, crediting runs again and inserts the reward; a third delivery finds the reward and does nothing.
  • Apple double-claim protection (task 20261001-owner-rewards-security-fixes). Problem: a promotional-offer signature stays redeemable at Apple after our own reservation lapses, so re-signing on lapse could let one reward yield two discounted months. Mechanism: (1) every signature's nonce is a fresh UUID stored in owner_rewards.apple_nonce (now UNIQUE where not null), also used as applicationUsername, so the transaction's appAccountToken identifies exactly which signature was redeemed. (2) New column apple_signature_expires_at = signing time + 24h Apple signature validity + 1h clock-skew margin (APPLE_SIGNATURE_VALID_HOURS, APPLE_SIGNATURE_SKEW_MARGIN_HOURS; protocol constants, signed timestamp and death time both come from the DB clock). The 24h validity is Apple's documented window and is the one external assumption here. (3) claim_apple returns 409 while ANY earned reward of the owner has a possibly-live signature, so OWNER_REWARD_APPLE_RESERVATION_MINUTES no longer gates re-issue (it still sets apple_reserved_until as an in-progress hint); only after the old signature is provably dead is the reward re-signed, replacing the ledger nonce so the old one can never finalize. _expire_due also skips rewards with a live signature so a reward cannot expire out from under a redeemable offer. A user who dismissed the sheet therefore waits up to about 25h (security preferred over convenience). (4) finalize_apple_claim(user, txn, product, offer, appAccountToken) locks the owner, is idempotent on the transaction id, finds the reward by (owner, apple_nonce = token) (stale, unknown, foreign or missing token matches nothing and is audited reward_apple_redeemed_unmatched), and claims with an atomic conditional UPDATE ... WHERE status='earned' AND apple_nonce=<token> (at most one finalization per reward; a second transaction with an already-finalized nonce is audited reward_apple_duplicate_redemption and grants nothing). Covers /apple/sync and /apple/notifications since both go through reconcile_apple_offer. All claim and finalize steps run under the per-owner pg_advisory_xact_lock. Migration: additive ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS apple_signature_expires_at plus a partial unique index on apple_nonce (db.py, idempotent). Backend only: iOS already passes the response's applicationUsername as appAccountToken.
  • Admin/user surface: admin-only creator-code creation attached to an email (secure generated FS- + 12 CSPRNG chars unless a code is supplied), deactivation, reactivation (only flips active; expiry/cap/creator checks still apply), soft delete of creator codes (promo_codes.deleted_at; friend codes rejected with 422; deleted codes vanish from lists/overview/validate/PATCH and reactivate is 404, but get_code_by_id still resolves them so in-flight checkouts log redemptions and rewards; text stays reserved; all idempotent, audited with ids only), and an overview with redemption and reward counts; promo_codes.owner_email is also set on a user's friend code (the existing POST /promo/{user_id}/friend-code is the invite-link endpoint). Admin authz reuses require_admin. Awaiting-email creator codes (task 20261005-creator-promo-awaiting-email): owner_email is optional on creator-code creation; blank creates the code deactivated with promo_codes.requires_owner_email = TRUE (additive column, default FALSE so legacy codes are untouched). awaiting_email (derived: flag set and no email) is exposed on code lists/overview. Activate/reactivate of such a code is 409; PATCH /admin/promo/codes/{id} accepts owner_email (format-checked, 422; blank removes it, which sets the flag and deactivates the code); saving an email never auto-activates. evaluate fails closed for flagged codes with no email even if active is true. Email set/removal is audited in promo_audit_log (ids only, no email).
  • Known limits: an iOS brand-new subscriber cannot receive a discount through our codes (Apple promotional offers are for existing/lapsed subscribers); they must subscribe on the web, where the first-month discount still applies. owner_email matching trusts that an account's email belongs to its holder (accounts are not email-verified), flagged for the security review. Invitees on the web keep the existing first-month 50% discount unchanged. Out of scope: payouts, group-plan rewards, auto-enabling the flag.

iOS friend-invite redemption via Apple offer codes (task 20261003-ios-friend-offer-code-redeem). Apple promotional offers only apply to current/lapsed subscribers, so a brand-new iOS subscriber redeems a friend code through an Apple offer code (offer eligibility "new subscribers", 50% off one month). Code: backend/subscription/apple_offer_codes.py (config, ASC client, OfferCodeManager, reconcile_offer_code), route POST /promo/{user_id}/ios-offer-code in routes/promo.py, reconcile hooks in routes/subscription.py (/apple/sync, /apple/notifications), table ios_offer_redemptions (schema_ddl/ios_offer_redemptions.py).

  • Manual prerequisite (the code never creates or edits an ASC offer). In App Store Connect create ONE offer code on com.fellowscript.access.one: customer eligibility New only, pay-as-you-go/pay-up-front 50% off for 1 period, one-time-use codes allowed. Note its reference name (must equal APPLE_OFFER_CODE_REFERENCE_NAME; StoreKit echoes it as offerIdentifier) and its subscriptionOfferCodes resource id (APPLE_OFFER_CODE_ID). The ASC API key (APPLE_ASC_KEY_ID/ISSUER_ID/KEY_PATH) must be allowed to create one-time-use codes. At runtime the server does a cached (10 min) read-only GET /v1/subscriptionOfferCodes/{id} and refuses to mint unless the offer is active, new-subscribers-only and the name matches. Until then the local .env holds placeholders for APPLE_ASC_ISSUER_ID and APPLE_OFFER_CODE_ID.
  • Config (env, no defaults, eagerly validated by validate_offer_codes_config() in the lifespan; three places: local .env, server ~/fellowscript-docker/.env (+ legacy ~/fellowscript/.env), CI env in build-push.yml): IOS_OFFER_CODES_ENABLED (deploy false; true also requires PROMO_CODES_ENABLED and OWNER_REWARDS_ENABLED), IOS_OFFER_CODE_EXPIRY_DAYS (7-180; pool batch validity), IOS_OFFER_CODE_RATE_LIMIT (per IP and per user), IOS_OFFER_CODE_IP_DAILY_CAP (issuances per HMAC-hashed client IP per 24h), IOS_OFFER_CODE_DAILY_MINT_CAP (global codes ISSUED per 24h), IOS_OFFER_CODE_BATCH_SIZE (codes per pool batch, 500-25000, default value 500), IOS_OFFER_CODE_DAILY_BATCH_CAP (ASC batch creations per 24h), APPLE_ASC_KEY_ID, APPLE_ASC_ISSUER_ID, APPLE_ASC_KEY_PATH (read only when enabled; never logged), APPLE_OFFER_CODE_ID, APPLE_OFFER_CODE_REFERENCE_NAME, APPLE_APP_STORE_ID. The app refuses to boot if any is missing, so set them on the server BEFORE deploying.
  • Flag off: the route is a uniform 404, reconcile hooks do nothing.
  • Validate then issue from a pool. OfferCodeManager.request_code reuses PromoManager.evaluate (code exists/active/unexpired/under cap, creator active, not the caller's own code, new subscriber by local history plus Stripe email lookup, TRIAL_MONTHS == 0), then requires a friend code, a client IP, an outstanding-aware cap (redemption_count + issued rows < max_redemptions), the per-IP and global issued-per-day caps. Every validation failure is the same 400 invalid_invite_code and makes no ASC call. Apple rejects one-time-use batches under 500 codes (live-tested 2026-10-04: numberOfCodes: 1 returns 409), so codes come from a POOL: ios_offer_batches rows (ASC batch id, size, expiry, next_index, ready_at). Only when no usable batch exists (none, exhausted, or expiring within a 3-day safety margin) does the server create one of IOS_OFFER_CODE_BATCH_SIZE codes via POST /v1/subscriptionOfferCodeOneTimeUseCodes; the row is committed pending before the call, creations are capped per day separately, and an unknown outcome blocks another create for an hour. ASC generates values asynchronously, so a batch is marked ready_at only once GET .../values returns the full count; until then requests get 503. Per issuance the server atomically takes the next index (next_index + 1 under an advisory lock, FOR UPDATE), stores only (batch, index) on the user's redemption row, reads the batch values from ASC (sorted, so an index is stable) and returns the code at that index. Code values are never stored or logged. Response: {offer_code, redeem_url, expires_at} (no-store); the iOS app opens AppStore.presentOfferCodeRedeemSheet (or redeem_url).
  • Seeding / adopting an existing ASC batch (operator step, one time). A batch created by hand in App Store Connect can be adopted instead of letting the server create one: insert a row into ios_offer_batches for it. The pool then uses it from index 0 and creates no other batch while it is active, has capacity and is not within 3 days of expiry. ready_at stays NULL; the first request reads GET .../values and marks it ready only if ASC returns exactly number_of_codes values (otherwise 503, fail closed). No code values are stored. Idempotent (unique index on asc_batch_id). Seed for the existing production batch 607166 (offer 0bb02306-84ae-4e7a-9826-ad5ab8e45e8e, 500 codes, expires 2027-01-02), run once on the server's database:

sql INSERT INTO ios_offer_batches (asc_batch_id, status, number_of_codes, next_index, expires_at) VALUES ('607166', 'active', 500, 0, '2027-01-02 23:59:59+00') ON CONFLICT (asc_batch_id) WHERE asc_batch_id IS NOT NULL DO NOTHING;

e.g. docker compose exec <db-service> psql -U <user> -d <db> -c "<the INSERT above>". Check with SELECT asc_batch_id, status, next_index, number_of_codes, ready_at FROM ios_offer_batches;. The table is created by create_tables at app startup, so seed after the first boot of this release. The batch's offer must be the configured APPLE_OFFER_CODE_ID. If ASC's batch resource id differs from the number shown in the console, the values fetch fails closed and the row can be corrected with an UPDATE of asc_batch_id. - Idempotency / failure modes. One live (pending|issued|redeemed) row per user (partial unique index) and one row per (batch, index) (unique). A retry while issued re-reads the SAME index, so a user never consumes a second code; redeemed is denied; an issued row past its expiry becomes expired and the user may be issued afresh. Failed rows (including the legacy single-code design's) never block a user; a legacy pending row is closed as failed. Pool exhaustion, ASC values not ready, a rejected or ambiguous batch create, the daily issued cap and the daily batch cap all fail closed with 503 and a promo_audit_log event, never a fabricated code. A reserved index whose values were not yet readable stays reserved for that user's retry. - Reward crediting only on the verified Apple transaction. reconcile_offer_code runs from /apple/sync and from OFFER_REDEEMED/SUBSCRIBED/DID_RENEW notifications (any transaction with an offerIdentifier), acts only on offerType == 3, offerIdentifier == APPLE_OFFER_CODE_REFERENCE_NAME, individual product. Correlation key: the transaction's user (sync: authenticated caller; notification: owner of the original transaction id) + that user's issued redemption row + offer identifier + transaction id (unique). Apple does not report which code was used, so a code handed to someone else matches no row for them and is audited ios_offer_redeemed_unmatched with no reward. On match: row -> redeemed, a promo_redemptions row (platform='apple', key ios-offer:<row id>, cap enforced atomically) and the owner reward via the same ledger as signups (key signup:<invitee id> plus the per-invitee/per-email unique indexes). A user who also sent invite_code at signup was already credited at signup, so the offer path cannot create a second reward. Replays complete any missed step and never duplicate (notification DB errors 500 so Apple retries; sync logs and the app re-syncs on launch). - Audit/redaction. promo_audit_log actions ios_offer_issued|expired|ip_capped|daily_capped|legacy_pending_closed|code_not_ready|pool_not_ready|pool_exhausted|batch_reserved|batch_created|batch_failed|batch_ambiguous|batch_pending_blocked|batch_capped|redeemed|redeemed_unmatched; ids only. ASC errors log the HTTP status only; no tokens, bodies or code values. - Known limits. Eligibility "new subscriber" is our check (local + Stripe) AND Apple's own offer eligibility; the ASC offer must be New-only or Apple will not enforce it. Offer-code redemption by someone other than the requesting account earns no owner reward (by design).

There is also a separate, admin-only plan_type='individual' row shape (provider='admin_comp'), unrelated to the old pre-GROUP_PRICE_CENTS "Individual" tier described above — it's a $0, non-billed grant created via POST /subscriptions/admin/grant-individual (require_admin) for the app's own admin account(s) to get free unlimited access without going through Stripe/Apple. See SubscriptionsManager.grant_admin_comp and the API reference.

Apple sync guards (three layers, spanning both POST /subscriptions/apple/sync and POST /subscriptions/apple/notifications): iOS reports every currently-active StoreKit entitlement (Transaction.currentEntitlements) to /apple/sync on each launch — a device/Apple-ID-level API, not scoped to whichever FellowScript account is signed in — and Apple's servers push renewal/refund/cancel events to /apple/notifications, which (like the Stripe webhook) has no user session and authenticates purely via the payload's own signature. 1. Signature verification (primary): apple_service.decode_jws verifies every JWS's x5c certificate chain against a pinned copy of Apple's Root CA - G3 before trusting any claim in the payload, then checks the ES256 signature itself. A JWS that doesn't chain to Apple's real root, or whose signature doesn't match, is rejected with ValueError (surfaced as 400) before its payload is ever read — closing both the authenticated-user-forges-their-own-sync and the unauthenticated-anyone-forges-a-notification paths. 2. Environment gate: every StoreKit transaction carries an environment ("Xcode" = local .storekit-file testing, "Sandbox" = TestFlight/App Review, "Production" = real purchase). The route calls apple_service.is_accepted_environment(...) and rejects with 400 before touching the DB unless it's Production (always) or Sandbox (gated by APPLE_ALLOW_SANDBOX, which must be explicitly "true" or "false" — the process refuses to start if it's unset, no implicit default). This is what stops a dev device's fabricated "Xcode" transaction (id "0") from turning every account signed in on that device into a paid plan — the actual cause of the repeated "new accounts show the paid plan" reports. 3. Ownership guard (defense-in-depth): upsert_from_apple still returns None → 409 if the apple_original_transaction_id is already tied to a different user_id, so one real transaction can't be spread across accounts.

docs.title: backend/email/
docs.text:
Transactional email delivery via AWS SES, used by the password-reset and 2FA flows.

File Responsibility ses_client.py send_email() — thin wrapper over boto3's sesv2 client; raises EmailSendError on failure. Uses a separate, narrowly-scoped IAM credential (SES_ACCESS_KEY_ID/SES_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY) from the Chime SDK user, per least-privilege. templates.py password_reset_email(), mfa_code_email(), mfa_setup_code_email() — each returns (subject, html_body, text_body). CAN-SPAM-compliant: truthful sender identity, a support contact, and a physical mailing address footer (SENDER_POSTAL_ADDRESS env var — must be set to a real address before sending real mail).

backend/auth/password_reset.py (PasswordResetManager) and backend/auth/mfa.py (MFAManager) generate the actual tokens/codes — both mirror SessionManager's pattern of storing only a sha256 hash, never the raw secret.

docs.title: backend/moderation/ — Guideline 1.2 (User-Generated Content)
docs.text:
File Responsibility content_filter.py check_clean(**fields) — severity-graded local content filter built on better_profanity's matching engine, raises ContentRejected(field, matched) on a match. Hard-rejects submission (422) rather than auto-flagging-and-posting. Wired into note/reply create+update (routes/notes.py), group title create+update (routes/community.py), devotion title+prompts create+update (routes/devotion.py), and the one non-HTTP path, ConnectionManager.send_msg (backend/interactions/websockets.py), which replies with an error frame to the sender's own socket instead of raising. As of 2026-08, ordinary profanity is allowed — only a curated _EXPLICIT_TERMS list (explicit sexual acts, sexual exploitation, hateful slurs) triggers a reject, not better_profanity's much broader default wordlist. Which tier of _SEVERITY_TIERS is active is controlled by the CONTENT_FILTER_SEVERITY env var (default "explicit"; an unrecognized value fails closed to the strictest known tier rather than silently loading an empty list). Every call site builds its 422/error-frame message via rejection_message(e), which names the specific flagged text (e.matched) in a warm, on-brand tone instead of a generic "contains language that isn't allowed" message. admin_actions.py CLI for resolving reports: python -m backend.moderation.admin_actions list / resolve <report_id> [--remove-content] [--eject] [--dismiss]. Removing content deletes/resets the note, message, devotion prompts, or group title by id; ejecting sets users.suspended_at and calls SessionManager.delete_all_for_user() to kill any active session immediately. No self-service admin UI exists yet — this is the "act within 24 hours" tool the report email points at.

Reporting — backend/interactions/reports.py (ReportsManager): create_report(content_type, content_id, reported_user_id, reason, detail) resolves the current author + text server-side (never trusts the client for who/what is reported), inserts a content_reports row with a frozen content_snippet (survives later edits/deletes), and emails SUPPORT_EMAIL via backend/email/templates.py's content_report_email() (HTML-escapes the snippet before interpolation). content_type is one of note / message / devotion_prompt / group_title / user.

Blocking — backend/interactions/blocks.py (BlockManager): block_user() severs any existing friendship/pending request both directions and auto-creates a content_reports row (reason='blocked') — one unified developer queue rather than a parallel notification system. is_blocked() checks both directions. Enforced at every read path a blocked relationship could otherwise leak through: friends.py's send_add_request/add_friend/read_friend/get_friend_activity (friend-activity dashboard feed — re-checks blocked_users both directions rather than trusting user_friends alone, same defense-in-depth as ActivityManager.friend_device_tokens), groups.py's fetch_notes/fetch_replies/fetch_group (member roster stays visible for transparency; only their content is hidden), websockets.py's send_msg (drops DMs entirely between blocked parties; skips delivery-only for group messages so other members still see them), and devotion.py's fetch_by_contact. Retroactively removing a blocked user from an already-joined live Chime call is a known, accepted gap.

docs.title: Messaging attachments (task 20260904-messaging-attachments)
docs.text:
A message may now carry an image/video/file/gif attachment alongside or instead of text — nullable attachment_kind / attachment_key / attachment_meta columns on the existing messages table (no new table). Handled entirely within the existing three-layer flow rather than a new subsystem:

File Responsibility backend/interactions/attachments.py Presigned S3 upload/download for image/video/file attachments only. generate_upload_policy(user_id, attachment_kind, content_type) issues a presigned S3 POST policy (not a bare PUT — only a POST policy's conditions can cryptographically bind content-length-range and an exact content-type) scoped to a server-derived object key (attachments/{user_id}/{uuid4()}{ext} — never a client-supplied filename/extension) and fails closed (ValueError) on any attachment_kind/content_type combination outside the per-kind allowlist (PER_KIND_LIMITS: image ≤15MB, video ≤250MB, file ≤50MB — a documented, deliberately curated MIME allowlist per kind, e.g. application/zip is excluded from "file" as a common malware vector). generate_download_url(object_key) issues a fresh, short-lived (1hr) presigned GET at read time — the object key itself is never handed to a client, only ever the DB-stored reference. Real size/content-type enforcement is the presigned POST policy (S3-enforced), not a server-side check a client could bypass by talking to S3 directly. Config (S3_BUCKET_NAME, S3_REGION env vars) is validated eagerly at startup via validate_attachment_config() (same main.py lifespan pattern as push.py's validate_apns_config) — an unconfigured deployment refuses to start. backend/interactions/gif_search.py Server-side GIF search proxy (GIPHY or Tenor, provider-agnostic behind one interface, selected via the GIF_PROVIDER env var) — settles the "client-direct vs. proxied" design question in favor of proxied: a client-side API key can't be kept both scoped and secret. search_gifs(query) returns only id/url/preview_url/width/height — never the provider's raw response (avoids forwarding provider tracking params). GIF bytes never touch our storage or attachments.py's limits at all — only the provider's own id/url is ever persisted, in attachment_meta. The API key (GIF_PROVIDER_API_KEY) loads via its own os.getenv call, is never logged, and never appears in an example config. validate_gif_config() is called eagerly at startup the same way as attachments.py's validator.

Wiring: POST /message/upload-url/{user_id} (self-scoped via require_match, rate-limited 30/min) issues the presigned upload policy; GET /message/gif-search?q= (authenticated, rate-limited 30/min) proxies a GIF search. Both live in routes/messaging.py alongside the existing ws_router. ConnectionManager.send_msg (backend/interactions/websockets.py) fails closed on an attachment-carrying payload whose attachment_kind isn't recognized or whose kind-specific reference (object key for image/video/file, provider url for gif) is missing — dropping the message entirely rather than persisting an ambiguous reference — and passes any user-supplied "file" attachment filename through check_clean alongside text, since it's just as much a free-text side channel. FriendsManager.read_friend and GroupsManager.format_messages both resolve attachment_key to a fresh presigned GET on every read, and the live WebSocket delivery frame does the same, so a stored/leaked object key alone never grants durable access. There is no malware/content scan of uploaded bytes in v1 (accepted, explicitly-tracked gap — GIFs are exempt since the provider already moderates its own catalog).

docs.title: Main-chat send guard (task 20261002-ws-send-hardening)
docs.text:
backend/interactions/send_guard.py (authorize_send) is the single owner of main-chat WebSocket send authorization, called once from ConnectionManager.send_msg before the block check and save_message. It is stateless; every query goes through the _GuardCursor adapter into ConnectionManager._execute, so stale-cursor repair applies. Group sends require a current, non-suspended member and derive recipients from the group's live member list (client to_users ignored). DMs require exactly one existing friend who is not the sender. image/video/file attachment keys must be under attachments/<sender_id>/. Outcomes:

Outcome Cause Sender sees SendDecision authorized normal send Reject genuine authorization denial (non-member, non-friend, forged recipients, foreign attachment key, bad group id) {type: error, reason: not_allowed} (uniform, cause logged internally only) Drop blocked DM nothing (silent, as before) Unavailable infrastructure failure inside the guard (database unreachable, query error, timeout) {type: error, reason: send_failed} (retriable)

Both Reject and Unavailable fail closed: the message is not saved. The split exists so an outage is never reported to users as "not allowed"; clients can retry send_failed but should not retry not_allowed.

docs.title: Group info panel (task 20260929-group-info-panel)
docs.text:
routes/group_info.py (/groups/{user_id}/{group_id}/...), all require_match + member-only (403 otherwise; any member may rename/change the photo, same as PUT /groups/{user_id}/{group_id}):

Method Path Purpose GET /info title, photo_url, caller's muted, member usernames PUT /title rename only ({"title"}; content filter, 1-255 chars after trim, else 422) POST /photo/upload-url presigned S3 POST for group-photos/{group_id}/{uploader}/{uuid} (image MIME/size allowlist reused) POST /photo/confirm persist {"object_key"}; 403 unless the key is under this group's prefix; replaced object deleted best-effort DELETE /photo clears the photo; returns {"restore_key"} and keeps the S3 object so the client can undo via /photo/confirm PUT / DELETE /mute per-user mute on/off (idempotent) GET /gallery?kind=&cursor_timestamp=&cursor_id= GALLERY_PAGE_SIZE (24) attachments, newest first, keyset-paged; has_more + next_cursor_*; blocked users excluded; URLs presigned at read time; kind in image/video/gif/file

GET /groups/{user_id}/{group_id} now also returns group.photo_url and group.muted (additive). PUT /groups/{user_id}/{group_id} now 422s a blank/overlong title. Push suppression: websockets.py::send_msg batches a group_mutes lookup and skips the APNs push (not WS/history delivery) for muted recipients; lookup errors fail open.

Migration/rollout plan: additive and idempotent via db.py (see data.md). Pre-flight: confirm groups/users exist and no group_mutes table conflicts (\d group_mutes). Deploy order: backend first (old clients ignore new fields), then clients. Rollback: drop group_mutes and groups.photo_key; old code never reads them. NOT to be run on production or deployed without explicit user confirmation; record the run (who/when) in the deploy log. Known gap: photo objects of removed/deleted groups are not swept (needs an S3 lifecycle rule or sweep job).

docs.title: backend/backup/
docs.text:
A sibling package to interactions/ for the nightly per-user data backup (see Data → Nightly Backup Database for the schema/scope).

File Responsibility manager.py BackupManager — holds two DB connections at once (source: primary fellowscript DB, dest: separate fellowscript_backup DB). users_due_now() finds users whose local time is currently 03:00; backup_user() copies that user's recent notes/verses and full highlights/bookmarks into the backup DB via upsert.

Unlike other managers, BackupManager doesn't subclass DBManager directly — it composes two DBManager instances (constructed via DBManager(dbname=...)) since it reads from one database and writes to another.

docs.title: db.py — Schema and DBManager
docs.text: create_tables() defines the full Postgres schema in FK-dependency order (Level 0 → Level 2). Additive ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS statements at the top of create_tables() handle live migrations without dropping data.

docs.title: Schema summary (Level 0 → 2)
docs.text:
Level 0 (no FK) - users — _id, username, email, hash_pass, apple_sub, google_sub, subscription_id, timezone - groups — _id, title, members UUID[], highlights JSONB - subscriptions — _id, user_id, plan_type, provider, status, price_cents, current_period_end, Stripe/Apple identifiers

Level 1 (FK → Level 0) - notes — _id, user_id, title, text, public, group_id, timestamp, created_at - messages — _id, from_user, group_id, content, is_dm, timestamp - highlights — (user_id, key) composite PK, color, timestamp (set on insert, refreshed on re-highlight) - bookmarks — (user_id, key) composite PK, label - notifications — _id, user_id, type, message, read - agents — _id, user_id, config JSONB - devotions — _id, creator_id, title, participants UUID[] - friend_requests — from_user_id, to_user_id - friend_list — user_id, friend_id

Level 2 (FK → Level 1) - note_verses — note_id, position, book, chapter, verse - agent_heartbeats — _id, user_id, last_fired, timeline_instruction - message_recipients — message_id, recipient_id

docs.title: Background Scheduler
docs.text:
backend/interactions/scheduler.py runs on startup (via lifespan), using APScheduler. Current jobs:

The former _fire_due_notifications job (fired user-authored "agentic" notifications on their scheduled time-of-day) was removed in full (2026-08-26) along with that subsystem, replaced by the fixed-notification jobs below (activity-tracked reminders + friend-went-active), backed by backend/interactions/activity.py's ActivityManager and user_activity table.

Job Cadence Does _run_nightly_backups every minute Copies any user whose local time is currently 03:00 into the backup database (see backend/backup/) _reconcile_trials every hour Advances elapsed trials to active, and removes subscriptions whose paid period lapsed past the grace window _run_error_watchdog every 90s Polls the 5 CloudWatch log groups the agent ships (nginx access/error, syslog, auth, app) via WatchdogManager.run_cycle, detects errors, assembles context, persists to error_detections, and triggers the debugging agent once per new detection (see backend/monitoring/ above) _fire_due_heartbeats every HEARTBEAT_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS (60s) Scans agent_heartbeats for any event whose UTC HH:mm slot for today has passed and hasn't fired yet, then fires it via AgentManager.commit_hb_response — the same atomic, per-calendar-day last_fired claim that route-triggered fires have always used remains the sole dedup mechanism, so a concurrent poll cycle or a stray client call can't double-fire. On a real fire, sends a push via send_push identifying the event generically (agent name only, never prompt/note content) with heartbeat_id/agent_id riding in the payload's data for the client to resolve locally. _midday_no_activity_reminder every 15 min Gentle nudge once a user's local clock reads noon and they've had no tracked activity (note/highlight) yet that day; deduped once/local-day via midday_reminder_sent_date _guilt_no_activity_reminder every 15 min More urgent nudge once a user has gone longer than 24h since their last tracked activity; deduped once per 24h window via guilt_reminder_sent_at _friend_went_active_notify every 5 min Notifies a user's friends (block-respecting both directions) the first time that user transitions from inactive (>24h) to active — not on every individual note/highlight/reply. The push body names the specific action via last_activity_type: "created a new note", "edited a note", "replied to {note owner}'s note" (NOTE_REPLIED — resolves the parent note's owner at send time), or a real-verse-content highlight line (VERSE_HIGHLIGHTED — resolves the user's most recent highlight and its verse text via the bundled bible_text module at send time; falls back to a reference-only or fully generic line if either lookup misses). Never logs note/highlight/verse content — that's only ever in the push body itself. _fire_due_session_reminders every SESSION_REMINDER_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS (60s, 2026-09-04) Scans devotions for any session whose time_start (absolute TIMESTAMPTZ) has passed and hasn't been reminded yet, atomically claims it (UPDATE devotions SET reminder_sent_at = NOW() WHERE reminder_sent_at IS NULL), then pushes every resolved member (DevotionManager.resolve_members — creator, participants, and the group/DM roster, the same membership concept is_authorized already encodes). One-shot dedup via reminder_sent_at, not a rolling time window — see devotions.reminder_sent_at. _advance_recurring_sessions every SESSION_RECURRING_ADVANCE_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS (60s, 2026-09-21) Scans devotions for any recurring = TRUE session whose time_end is more than SESSION_RECURRING_ADVANCE_GRACE_SECONDS (1h) in the past, gates on the same fail-closed AWS Chime presence check the auto-delete job uses, then advances time_start/time_end in place by exactly one calendar week — computed in the session creator's own local timezone (users.timezone, zoneinfo-aware, so a DST transition doesn't shift the wall-clock time) rather than a raw 7-day UTC offset. The same atomic UPDATE also resets reminder_sent_at to NULL (so the advanced occurrence's start-time push re-arms) and chime_meeting_id/chime_meeting to their column defaults (''/{}, so the new occurrence never inherits a finished call's meeting state), re-checking the row's time_end at write time to avoid a double-advance across concurrent poll cycles. A non-recurring session is never touched by this job; a malformed time_end or an unresolvable creator timezone is a fail-closed skip, not a guess. No push/websocket notification of the new time is sent — clients pick it up on their next session fetch. run_join_request_sweeper_job every 10 min (2026-10-02) Thin async def; join_request_sweeper.sweep_once runs in an executor: expires stale and ownerless pending join requests and purges decided rows past retention; runs even with flag join_requests off (see Join requests below)

Heartbeat (AI agent event) firing is now scheduled server-side by _fire_due_heartbeats above — it fires on time whether or not any client has the app open. The former client-side trigger, iOS's HeartbeatScheduler (scheduleAll/checkAndFire, polled on scenePhase foreground), was removed in full (2026-09-01); commit_heartbeat itself is unchanged and still does the actual generation/persistence work, just no longer reachable from iOS.

Heartbeat timeline instructions (2026-09-06). Each heartbeat's future note content is now planned upfront rather than deduped reactively — see agent_heartbeats.timeline_instruction for the storage shape. AgentManager.add_heartbeat calls a dedicated timeline-planning LLM prompt (backend/interactions/timeline_prompt.txt, distinct from the note-writing agent's own agent_prompt.txt) synchronously at creation time — a heartbeat row is never inserted without a timeline, and generation failure (TimelineGenerationError, mapped to a 502 by an app-wide handler in main.py) aborts the whole create. At fire time, commit_hb_response/_commit_hb_response_forced call AgentManager.ensure_current_timeline immediately after winning their respective fire claim (the unforced path's last_fired UPDATE, or the forced path's advisory lock) — this regenerates the plan only if it's missing or its window has elapsed, informed by the outgoing plan's coverage_summary so the new window doesn't repeat old content, and is safe against two racing fires since only the claim-winner ever reaches it. update_heartbeat nulls timeline_instruction whenever timestamps changes, so a schedule edit falls through to the same lazy regeneration path on the heartbeat's next fire. _generate_and_save_note reads that day's specific instruction off the current timeline instead of the old agentic_context-backed CHAPTERS/VERSES/THEME aggregate, which was removed in full along with AgentManager.save_context/get_context and scripts/migrate_agentic_context_categories.py.

docs.title: backend/interactions/bible_text.py
docs.text: In-process, lazily-loaded lookup over a bundled static copy of bible.json (the same asset the iOS Bible reader ships, copied into api/backend/interactions/bible_data/bible.json) — no database table, no outbound network call, since the content never changes at runtime. Exposes verse_text(book, chapter, verse) -> str | None (parses a chapter's flowing-text blob into per-verse strings on first access, cached after) and parse_highlight_key(key) -> (book, chapter, verse) | None (splits a highlights.key value back into its parts). Both return None on any miss rather than raising; callers (the friend-went-active push job, FriendsManager.get_friend_activity) fall back to reference-only or fully generic text.

docs.title: Group invite links (task 20260929-group-invite-links)
docs.text:
routes/invites.py + backend/interactions/invites.py (InvitesManager, per-kind handler registry; only 'group' today so phase 2 subscription-seat invites add a handler, no schema change). invites table (db.py): SHA-256 token hash only (256-bit CSPRNG tokens, plaintext returned once at creation), kind, untyped target_id (no FK; group delete/last-leave purges its invites in code), expires_at, max_uses, use_count, revoked_at. Redeem locks the group row, rejects blocked pairs (either direction, any current member), then a single UPDATE ... WHERE use_count < max_uses AND not expired/revoked RETURNING gates the join in the same transaction as the member append. Tunables and the feature flag (enabled, turned on 2026-09-30) live in api/config/invites.json, validated at startup (invites_config.py, no implicit defaults). Audit lines INVITE_AUDIT ... log only an 8-char hash prefix, never the token.

Permanent group links and member cap (task 20260930-group-invite-permanent-member-cap). Group (kind 'group') links never expire: invites.expires_at is now nullable and group links store NULL (handler permanent = True; a client-sent expires_in_days is ignored). Usable-token SQL is (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > NOW()); existing group links keep their original expiry, and subscription links always keep a non-null expiry. Group default_expiry_days/allowed_expiry_days are deprecated (still required and validated so boot never breaks, but unused for groups). groups.max_members (nullable, NULL = unlimited) is the owner-set cap: PUT /groups/{user_id}/{group_id}/max-members ({"max_members": int|null}, creator only: 403 otherwise, 422 for non-int/bool, outside [2, max_group_members_ceiling], or below the current member count; audited as INVITE_AUDIT event=set_max_members). New required key max_group_members_ceiling in api/config/invites.json (250). GET /groups/{user_id}/{group_id}/info adds max_members, member_count, is_owner, max_members_ceiling. Enforcement: invite redeem checks the cap under the group row lock (409 group_full; existing members stay idempotent; preview treats a full group as the uniform not_found), with a SQL guard in the append as defense in depth; PUT /groups/{user_id}/{group_id} (member-list replace) also locks the row and returns 409 group_full when it would add members past the cap.

Member removal revokes that member's group links (task 20261002-revoke-leaving-member-invite-links). Group links are permanent, so a link must not outlive its creator's membership. revoke_member_group_invites(cur, group_id, member_ids) (backend/interactions/invites.py) sets revoked_at = NOW() (the same state manual revoke/reset use, no new state) on that member's active kind='group' links for the group, never touching 'subscription' links; it only matches revoked_at IS NULL so it is idempotent, and logs INVITE_AUDIT event=auto_revoke with counts only (no tokens). It runs on the caller's cursor inside the same transaction, under the groups row FOR UPDATE lock that redeem and the member cap take first (lock order: group row, then invite rows, so no deadlock and a concurrent redeem either lands before the departure or finds the link revoked). Callers: GroupsManager.leave_group (now one transaction: lock, member list update, revoke, commit; the creator is treated like any other member, so a leaving creator's links are now revoked, a change from before) and GroupsManager.update_group (the PUT member-list replace revokes the links of every dropped member in the same transaction as the write; retained members keep theirs). These are the only writers that remove from groups.users (there is no separate owner-removal endpoint). Any failure rolls back both the membership change and the revoke (fail closed, SaveFailedError). Group delete and last-member leave still hard-delete all the group's invites (purge_target_invites; the last-member path is now in the same transaction as the group delete). A revoked link returns the same responses as any other revoked link. Rejoining never resurrects a revoked link.

Backfill and deploy runbook note. db.backfill_revoke_departed_group_invites(cur) revokes every active kind='group' link whose creator is no longer in that group's users (left or removed before this fix, or whose group is gone). It is idempotent (a second run matches nothing), additive, and is called from create_tables, so it changes production data on the first startup after the next deploy (a one-time revocation of orphaned links; log line INVITE_AUDIT event=backfill_revoke_departed count=N). Nothing was run against production in this task.

Reveal ("Show link") for group links (task 20261002-group-invite-show-link). New group links get an HMAC-derived token so they can be re-shown: create stores a random 32-byte invites.reveal_nonce (new nullable BYTEA, ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS in create_tables) and the token is base64url_nopad(HMAC-SHA256(INVITE_LINK_SECRET, nonce)) (43 chars, 256-bit, same _TOKEN_RE). The SHA-256 token_hash is stored exactly as before, so preview/redeem/revoke are unchanged; the HMAC output is never stored, so a DB leak alone cannot reconstruct any link. reveal_nonce IS NULL means legacy (random token, unrecoverable) or subscription; those keep working for redeem but cannot be revealed. GET /invites/{user_id}/{invite_id}/reveal (authenticated, Cache-Control: no-store, gated by the enabled flag, limited by rate_limits.reveal and reveal_per_user) returns {invite_id, url} only for an active (not revoked/expired/exhausted) derived group link, to a current group member who is the link's creator or the group manager. Every failure (bad id, unknown, subscription, inactive, legacy, non-member, neither creator nor manager, or a recomputed token whose hash no longer matches the stored hash) returns the one uniform 404 not_found; the match is checked with hmac.compare_digest. Audit: INVITE_AUDIT event=reveal ... as=creator|manager (ids and 8-char ref only) and event=reveal_miss reason=<code> server-side only; the token is never logged. GET .../groups/{group_id} list items gain an additive boolean revealable (clients show "created before reveal was available - create a new link" when false). Config: INVITE_LINK_SECRET (env, required, >=32 chars, no default; validate_invite_link_secret() runs in the lifespan and the app refuses to boot without it; the value is never logged or echoed). Three places: local .env, server ~/fellowscript/.env (manual step, needs explicit confirmation before the first deploy of this change), and the CI env block in build-push.yml. Rotation: changing the secret does not affect redeem/preview/revoke (hash only) but makes reveal fail (uniform 404) for every previously derived link; users then create new links. No key-versioning column (rotation only degrades reveal).

Subscription-seat invites (phase 2, kind 'subscription'; supersedes "only 'group' today" above). Handlers implement a kind-neutral interface (lock_target, is_actor, is_manager, create_precheck, existing_outcome, redeem_precheck, apply, preview, purge); the group handler's behavior is unchanged. target_id = subscriptions._id. Only the plan owner (subscriptions.user_id) can create/list/revoke/reset links (403 otherwise, including plan members), and only on an active, non-lapsed group plan with max_members > 1 (409 not_eligible otherwise). Routes: POST|GET /invites/{user_id}/subscriptions/{subscription_id}, POST .../reset; preview/redeem/revoke are shared. Redeeming never changes users.subscription_id: it inserts a pending subscription_request (idempotent; a link use is consumed only when a new request row is created) that the owner accepts or declines via the existing /subscriptions/{id}/requests endpoints. Redeem rejects (uniform not_found) a plan that is ineligible, full, or at its pending-request cap; 409 other_plan if the caller already sits on a different non-free plan; 403 blocked for a block in either direction with the owner or any member. An existing member (incl. the owner) gets already_member; an existing pending request gets pending with no use consumed. Public preview returns only {kind, inviter_username, plan_type}. SubscriptionsManager.accept_request now runs in one transaction under SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the subscriptions row (same lock redeem takes), so concurrent accepts cannot exceed max_members, and it refuses a requester who has since joined another paid plan. Subscription invites are purged in the same transaction as plan deletion (incl. lapse/cancel) and on downgrade to a single seat. New invites.json keys (required, validated at startup): subscription_default_expiry_days, subscription_allowed_expiry_days, subscription_default_max_uses, subscription_allowed_max_uses, max_active_links_per_subscription, max_pending_requests_per_subscription. Audit (INVITE_AUDIT, ids/8-char refs only): create/redeem/redeem_noop/redeem_fail/revoke/reset plus subscription_request_accept[_fail], subscription_request_decline, subscription_request_cancel. Residual (flagged for security review): the open POST /subscriptions/{id}/requests still lets any authenticated user request by plan id, and GET .../requests still returns requester email to the owner.

docs.title: Shared foundation (task 20261002-shared-foundation)
docs.text:
Cross-cutting plumbing every later feature task builds on. Ships inert: all flags seed off.

  • DDL modules. api/schema_ddl/<name>.py (each exposes apply(cur)); db.DDL_MODULES lists them, one name per line, and create_tables applies them in order at its end, in the same boot transaction. An unknown module raises. Before the first module the runner sets lock_timeout to 30 s (transaction-local), so a boot blocked behind another session fails loudly instead of hanging under restart: unless-stopped. Deploys stay stop-then-start. Modules: flags, outbox, chat_pagination, listings.
  • Feature flags (backend/interactions/flags.py, table feature_flags). States off/canary/on; registry attributes no_canary (explorer_browse is off/on only) and exposed_in_capabilities. One query reads every row, cached 10 s per process (single uvicorn process); fail closed (any DB error means every flag off, one WARNING per minute); invalidate() after a write. Flip with PUT /admin/flags/{name} or python -m backend.admin_flags. Claude and the pipeline never flip flags.
  • GET /app/capabilities (routes/app_capabilities.py): per-user feature booleans from the flag registry, links.explore, terms_current. See the API overview.
  • Config sections (backend/config_loader.py load_section): the invites_config rules (every key required, unknown and wrong-typed rejected, rate strings parsed with limits.parse, no implicit defaults). backend/startup_checks.py validate_all() runs from the lifespan; one check per line in CHECKS.
  • Paging (backend/interactions/paging.py): the one cursor codec (encode_cursor, decode_cursor(params, id_type, with_seq), clamp_limit, envelope). Text ids match ^[0-9A-Za-z]{10}$ and bind as %s::text; uuid ids bind as %s::uuid; malformed input is 422 before SQL.
  • Terms gate (backend/auth/terms.py): terms_current(cur, user_id) and require_current_terms(cur, user_id) (403 terms_reaccept_required).
  • FEATURE_SUMMARY (backend/observability/feature_summary.py): one hourly INFO line of counts only (public requests, 404s, 429s, shed requests, statement timeouts, probe-off hits, outbox backlog, pending join requests). It is the only visibility surface for 429 and probe traffic, which are deliberately not logged per request. Counts only, no ids or PII.

docs.title: Lifecycle hooks, S3 outbox and group member hygiene (shared foundation, step 3)
docs.text:
• Lifecycle registries (backend/interactions/lifecycle.py): four registries, group_delete, member_leave, user_delete and listing_hidden, with register(kind, fn) and run(kind, cur, ...). Hooks run in the caller's open transaction and return S3 keys; the caller enqueues them with enqueue_s3_deletes. A hook that raises aborts the whole delete (chosen over silently losing keys). SF registers the group photo and announcement banner collectors (only keys the owning helper can prove belong to that group) and the user_delete member removal in backend/lifecycle_wiring.py, which imports other feature modules only at function level (groups.py imports lifecycle).
  • Outbox (pending_s3_deletes, DDL module outbox, backend/interactions/s3_outbox.py): request paths (delete_group, leave_group, delete_user) only INSERT keys in the same transaction and never flush. A 60 s scheduler job (thin async def, work via run_in_executor) claims up to 200 rows FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, deletes each object, drops the row on success and counts an attempt otherwise; rows at 20 attempts are given up on and kept. One aggregated WARNING per run with counts; at most one S3_DELETE_DENIED ERROR per key prefix per 24 h. The IAM user needs s3:DeleteObject on group-photos/* and group-announcements/* (action A1a) or every attempt is an aggregated AccessDenied. attachments.delete_object (single key, best effort) is unchanged and is not used by the outbox.
  • One transaction body for leaving. GroupsManager.remove_member_in_tx(cur, group_id, user_id) is exactly the leave_group body (array remove, invite revoke, member_leave hooks, or last-member group delete with group_delete collectors and invite purge). leave_group and the user_delete hook both call it. delete_group now collects keys, enqueues, deletes the row and purges invites in one transaction.
  • Account deletion (DELETE /user/{id}): before the user row goes, the user_delete hook removes the id from every group's member list (a last-member group is deleted). Before this, deleted ids stayed in groups.users and made later group sends fail. Existing dangling ids are cleaned by the operator-run python -m backend.maintenance.prune_group_members (dry run by default; --apply is one idempotent UPDATE that keeps array order; groups left empty are reported, never deleted).
  • Member validation. PUT /groups/{user_id}/{group_id} drops ids that are already in the stored list but no longer exist (so build-78 clients that echo the raw array keep working). A NEW id must be a UUID of an existing, non-suspended user, otherwise 422 {"code": "invalid_member"} (same body for malformed, unknown and suspended ids: no existence oracle). POST /groups/{user_id} applies the same rule to every supplied id (the creator's own id always passes).
  • Live member helper. groups.LIVE_MEMBER_JOIN and groups.live_member_ids(cur, group_id) are the only place the groups.users to users join is written. The users side is matched with a CASE-guarded uuid cast of the array element (never u._id::text = x, which full-scans users; the CASE also stops a junk string raising a cast error). Readers (message authorship, recipients, member counts) import it.
  • Report and moderation registries. reports.CONTENT_RESOLVERS[type](cur, content_id, reported_user_id) returns (author_id, snippet, canonical_content_id) or None (not found: the route answers 404 and stores nothing); backend/moderation/removers.CONTENT_REMOVERS[type](cur, content_id) replaces the CLI's if/elif chain (kept in its own module so the python -m run does not create a second registry). The five original types keep their lenient behaviour. content_type also accepts group_listing and thread_message (no resolver yet, so 404 until LST and THR register theirs). A malformed content_id is 422 (it used to be a 500); group_listing ids must match ^[0-9A-Za-z]{10}$.
  • backend/registrations.py load_all() imports every module that registers hooks, resolvers or removers; main.py (lifespan) and backend.moderation.admin_actions call it because the CLIs are separate processes. A content type with no registered remover makes the CLI exit non-zero instead of removing nothing. Later tasks add one import line each.

docs.title: Logging convention (C19) and the CloudWatch watchdog
docs.text:
The watchdog (backend/monitoring/watchdog.py) treats the bare word ERROR at any level as a detection, and each detection can cost an LLM triage call.

  1. ERROR only for unexpected failures (DB write failure keeps its DB_WRITE_FAILURE marker; unhandled exceptions).
  2. Expected denials, uniform 404s, flag-off hits, rate-limit hits, validation failures and public query timeouts are INFO or not logged. Text of non-error lines says "failed", never the bare word ERROR.
  3. Retries and partial failures in sweepers, the outbox and notifiers: one WARNING per run with counts, never per key or per recipient.
  4. At most one S3_DELETE_DENIED ERROR per prefix per 24 h.
  5. No usernames, emails, message or listing text, cursor values or presigned URLs in any line; ids only.

nginx access-log rule. The watchdog also scans /fellowscript/nginx/access every 90 s: every 5xx line is a per-line http_5xx detection and 30 4xx lines in a window raise a 4xx anomaly (up to 25 LLM triage calls per cycle). So public surfaces answer an expected "off" state with 200 and a body (never 404), and shed load with 429 plus Retry-After (never 503).

docs.title: Rules for new code
docs.text:
• R-SCHED. Every new scheduler job is a thin async def registered with scheduler.add_job(..., id=..., replace_existing=True); all psycopg2, boto3 and SES work runs through await loop.run_in_executor(None, sync_fn); one aggregated WARNING per run with counts; no per-key or per-recipient log lines.
  • R-ROUTE. New authenticated routes are plain def (FastAPI runs them in the threadpool), because some take FOR UPDATE locks and a lock wait on the event loop would freeze every WebSocket. Public routes use run_public (added later in this task). Existing async def routes are not rewritten.

docs.title: Edge and runtime hardening (step 5)
docs.text:
• Client IP. backend/rate_limiting.py get_client_ip trusts CF-Connecting-IP only when the TCP peer is loopback (nginx) or the test client, and only when the value parses as an IP; otherwise the peer is the rate-limit key. X-Real-IP is never read. The Dockerfile starts uvicorn with --no-proxy-headers so the peer is not rewritten; the two must ship together. ops/nginx/real-ip.conf (prepared, not applied) makes nginx overwrite the header.
  • WebSocket registry. ConnectionManager.disconnect(user_id, ws) removes an entry only if that socket is still the registered one, so an old socket's cleanup cannot evict a newer connection. The heartbeat loop calls evict_suspended() about once a minute and closes sockets of suspended accounts with code 1008.
  • Public API isolation. backend/public_guard.py runs public handlers' blocking work on a dedicated anyio.CapacityLimiter (configure(concurrency, max_waiting) once at startup, no defaults). Overload and statement timeouts answer 429 {"code": "busy"} with Retry-After, never 5xx (the watchdog scans nginx 5xx lines); timeouts are summarised in one WARNING per minute.
  • Password check. backend/auth/passwords.py verify_password returns False for an empty or invalid hash, so /login and /auth/mfa/disable return the usual 401 for Apple and Google accounts instead of a 500.
  • Watchdog. _HTTP_4XX_QUERY excludes /api/explorer/ and /api/auth/apple-web/ so expected 404 and 429 there cannot trip the 4xx anomaly.

docs.title: Explorer listings (task 20261001-explorer-listings, backend A)
docs.text:
Text-only listing core; all behaviour behind the explorer_publish flag (owner routes) and explorer_browse (public probe), both off by default.

  • Data. group_listings (one row per group, own table so the public/private boundary stays explicit) and an empty group_listing_media, created by DDL module listings (see api/schema_tree.md). Search uses a generated simple tsvector over scalar columns plus an app-maintained description_text.
  • Config. api/config/explorer.json section listings (backend/interactions/listings_config.py): vocabularies, limits, rate limits, youth-term list, blocked link hosts, approval switch, public-API tunables. Every key required, validated at startup through startup_checks, which also calls public_guard.configure(...).
  • Code. backend/interactions/listing_content.py (validation/normalisation: controlled vocab, plain-text rules, restricted Markdown blocks, check_clean, youth terms), listings.py (lifecycle state machine, owner manager, moderation transitions and the shared helpers public_where, listing_requestable, set_accepting_requests, get_accepting_requests, group_has_explorer_presence, live_member_count, requeue_for_review), listings_wiring.py (lifecycle hooks, loaded by registrations.load_all), listing_sweeper.py (scheduler job that hides listings whose owner was suspended or left), routes/explorer.py.
  • Public read side (backend B). backend/interactions/listings_public.py + schemas/explorer_public.py (allowlisted pydantic models built field by field). Thin async def routes call public_guard.run_public; each call opens its own connection via public_guard.public_connection (SET LOCAL statement_timeout). Every query is built on listings.public_where(); facets use GIN &&, q uses search_tsv @@ plainto_tsquery('simple', ...); the keyset is (published_at, public_id) through paging.decode_cursor(id_type='text', with_seq=False). Size bucket and open/full come from one lateral count over groups.LIVE_MEMBER_JOIN inside the list query, so statements per request do not grow with page size.
  • Visibility. One SQL fragment, listings.public_where, is the authority: published AND the group's creator exists, is still a member and is not suspended. Ambiguity hides. Suspending an owner hides their listings immediately; the sweeper then updates the stored state and fires listing_hidden hooks (fn(cur, group_id, reason)).
  • PUT /groups guard. GroupsManager.update_group refuses (409 owner_only) non-creator additions and creator removal while the group has a listing in review, published or hidden.

docs.title: Message threads and message delete (task 20261001-message-threads)
docs.text: Two capabilities behind two DB flags, threads and message_delete (both off by default; only the owner flips them). Tunables live in api/config/chat.json sections threads and message_delete (backend/interactions/threads_config.py, every key required, validated at startup).

docs.title: Message delete (flag message_delete)
docs.text:
• Routes (routes/messages_delete.py, plain def): DELETE /groups/{user_id}/{group_id}/messages/{message_id} and POST .../restore. Author only, while still a current, non-suspended member of the message's group; groups only. Each is ONE atomic UPDATE (author, group match, live membership through a CASE-guarded uuid cast, author not suspended, state), so every failure (flag off, malformed or unknown id, not the author, not a member, wrong group, already deleted, outside the undo window) is the same 404. Not gated by require_current_terms: a delete is not new content.
  • Soft delete and undo. deleted_at/deleted_by are set at once and every reader hides the row. undo_seconds (10) governs restore only; text and the S3 object are kept.
  • Evidence retention. reports._resolve_message has no deleted_at filter, so a report filed after the delete still captures the text. The sweeper (message_delete.purge_once, a thin async def job every 15 minutes, work in run_in_executor, runs even while the flag is off) purges a row only after evidence_retention_days (30) and only when no content_reports row for it is open: it clears the text and attachment columns and threads.root_preview, and queues the S3 key in pending_s3_deletes only when the key is under the author's own attachments/<author_id>/ prefix and no other messages or thread_messages row uses it. One aggregated WARNING per run, never a per-key line.
  • Frames. {"type":"message_deleted","id","group_id","deleted_at"} and {"type":"message_restored", id, group_id, sender, body, created_at, seq, attachment_*} go best-effort to live members (restore skips block relationships). Neither carries from_user or text, so build 78 ignores them.
  • Rate limits use limiter.shared_limit(..., scope=<fixed name>, key_func=<per user>). slowapi buckets by URL path unless a shared scope is given, so a per-user limit on a path with an id parameter needs a fixed scope or each id gets its own bucket (this was fixed here and in the Explorer owner routes).
  • Rollback. Turn the flag off (effective within 10 s). Soft-deleted rows stay hidden. After the first use, roll the image back only to one that already contains the deleted_at filters.

docs.title: Threads (flag threads)
docs.text:
• Data. threads, thread_messages, thread_followers (DDL module threads, see api/schema_tree.md). Thread messages are in their own table, never in messages, so no legacy reader needs a filter. One thread per root message (partial unique index), groups only, no nesting, no close (a thread dies with its group or by an explicit delete, below). A deleted root leaves the thread alive with root_deleted: true and no preview.
  • Routes (routes/threads.py, plain def, group_info.py untouched): POST /groups/{user_id}/{group_id}/threads, GET .../threads, GET .../threads/{thread_id}/messages, PUT .../threads/{thread_id} (see the API overview). Logic is in backend/interactions/threads.py (ThreadsManager).
  • Authorization. Every call re-reads membership through send_guard.is_current_member (groups.live_member_ids), resolves a thread id to its own group_id and compares it with the path, and takes visibility from groups.author_set (caller plus current members, minus both-direction blocks). Every denial is one 404 (flag off, malformed id, non-member, another group's thread or message, a root whose author the caller cannot see, rename by a non-creator). Create answers 403 terms_reaccept_required through require_current_terms after membership is established; rename, read and list are not terms-gated.
  • Create takes a per-group advisory lock, so concurrent creates for one root give one thread and the per-group cap (max_threads_per_group, 409 thread_limit) holds. Creator and root author become followers. A blank title is auto-generated from the root text (auto_title_length) or Photo/Video/GIF/File; titles pass check_clean.
  • Per-user limits use shared_limit with fixed scopes (thread_create, thread_rename, threads_list, thread_messages_page); the WebSocket send limit is limiter.limiter.hit with scope thread-send.
  • Send path (backend/interactions/thread_send.py). The frame {type:'thread_message', thread_id, text, client_ref?, attachment_kind?, attachment_key?, attachment_meta?} reaches it through ONE dispatch branch in routes/messaging.py; ConnectionManager.send_msg is unchanged. The group and recipients come from the thread through send_guard.resolve_main_chat_recipients (never the client's group_id/to_users/from_user); the attachment key goes through send_guard.validate_attachment_key; then the content filter, the sender's block set and ONE statement through ConnectionManager._execute (reconnect and retry) that inserts the row, bumps last_activity_at and adds the sender as a follower. Error frames to the sender only: not_allowed (uniform: flag off, bad frame, unknown thread, non-member, suspended, foreign key), rate_limited, terms_reaccept_required, message_rejected, send_failed, message_not_saved.
  • Frames out. Ack: {type:'ack', client_ref, id, group_id, thread_id, timestamp} to the sender. Live: {type:'thread_message', thread_id, group_id, id, sender, body, created_at, seq, attachment_kind, attachment_meta, attachment_url} to online current members except the sender and blocked pairs. It has type and neither from_user nor text, so build 78 and the previous web bundle ignore it.
  • Push. Followers only, offline only, not blocked, not the sender, not group-muted (mute lookup fails open, like send_msg). Data {action:'thread_message', group_id, thread_id}, identifiers only.
